To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cut capacity on a graph is a good approximation for the perimeter in the continuum setting, provided that the graph is constructed using a suitable scaling of the neighborhood size, and that the metric used to compare the functionals is a transportation based metric.

the cut capacity, or more generally the total variation, on graphs obtained as random samples is a good approximation to the perimeter in the continuum setting, and that the approximation improves as the number of data points increases.

(a) we have developed a new transportation-based metric to study point clouds, (b) we have proved that the graph cut capacity, as the size of the neighbourhood over which points are connected increases, converges to the perimeter in the continuum setting, and (c) we have proved a Γ-convergence result for the cut capacity in the setting of random point clouds.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing mathematical tools for the study of graph-based algorithms for clustering.
the development and analysis of tools for the mathematical analysis of machine learning algorithms on point clouds.
the study of the consistency, as data increases, of graph based machine learning algorithms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the graph cut capacity, and total variation, converge to the total variation in the continuum as the number of data points goes to infinity, if the size of the neighborhoods over which points are connected is scaled to zero at a rate that is slower than the number of points.
if a point cloud is sufficiently dense and the size of the neighborhoods is sufficiently small, then the total variation on the graph converges to the total variation of the underlying measure.
the cut capacity, suitably rescaled, converges to the perimeter, suitably rescale, of the support of a measure on the Euclidean domain as the number of data points increases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we develop a theory of Γ-convergence on point clouds, and apply it to the problem of consistency of graph-based algorithms.
we develop a mathematical framework for studying the convergence of the graph-based machine learning methods.
the cut capacity on the graph is a good approximation to the perimeter in the continuum setting if the number of points grows proportionally to the number of edges in the graph.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cut capacity and more general total variation on point clouds is a consistent approximation of the perimeter in the continuum.

the cut capacity and total variation on the graph are a good approximation to the continuum perimeter, provided that the number of points is large enough and the size of the neighborhoods over which the points in the graph are connected is sufficiently small.
, in order to recover the continuum limit of the cut capacity, the number of points must be large enough to ensure that the points are connected with a large enough neighborhood.
